v1.kill_reason: The reference is a one-line upstream semantic change (PR #106226) plus two public neighbouring commits, far below the required hundreds of lines and too small for a 4 h tier. Its core fix is merged in public history and recallable, so the scope is one lever in disguise. A redesign with a larger real surface would be needed to pass.

spike_plan.kill_if: Build fails or exceeds 2 hours, or the only measurable gain is the one-line get_child_count change with nothing else to optimise (confirming K10).
spike_plan.pass_if: Build completes in under 90 minutes and the PR's change plus neighbours yields a measurable speedup while the unit tests stay green, AND a credible set of 10+ further tree operations exists with separable gains.
steps: In a throwaway networked container, clone godotengine/godot and check out a377f50^ (the PR parent); do not keep history in /app.
Run a headless scons build (target=template_release, tests=yes) with -j8 and record wall time and whether it completes.
Write a 50-line microbenchmark: build a tree of ~10k nodes, loop get_child_count(true) and get_child_count(false) plus get_node by path, time before and after applying the PR's one-line change.
Run the trimmed Godot scene/node unit tests on both builds to confirm they pass identically.
Check whether the measured speedup from the PR alone exceeds noise (median of 5 runs); if it does, sketch 3-5 further tree operations to see whether a larger scope exists.

v1.summary: The source PR #106226 exists and is merged upstream (commit a377f50, MIT repo), so the reference is public history and its core change is a one-line semantic tweak. The seed's 4 h tier and multi-operation framing are not supported by a reference this small, and the smoke build was never run, so I kill it as K10 (one lever, reference too small) unless the scope is rebuilt around a larger real surface.
